chunks: (And told:) "Eat and drink to your fill as reward for (good) deeds you had done in days of yore."
ai.seo_question: Why do the righteous eat and drink in Paradise according to the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-Waqi'ah highlights the direct causal link between earthly worship and eternal bliss, emphasizing that the 'good deeds' (hasanat) performed in the 'days of yore' are the sole basis for this divine invitation. Scholars note that the phrase 'haneean' (with pleasure) signifies not just physical satisfaction but a spiritual contentment derived from the sincerity of one's past actions, reinforcing the concept of divine justice where effort is rewarded without measure.
